solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Share the cost of a trip to Amsterdam?

definitions.meaning: to split a bill so each person pays their own part
a jokey literal reading: to travel to the Netherlands, home of the Dutch

explanation.definitionFit: Paying separately is the idiom; heading to Holland is the literal phrase taken at its word.

clue.text: One with a lot of neck in blunder involving taxman

definitions.text: One with a lot of neck

indicators.note: involving means wrapping around the other piece

parts.note: a gaffe is a social blunder
IR is the Inland Revenue, the former British tax authority

explanation.surface: A tax inspector caught in an embarrassing slip-up, showing some cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-necked African animal literally has a great deal of neck; neck also means cheek.

clue.text: Regret James turning up second at one's party

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning up means reading the name bottom to top

parts.note: Sid James was a British comic actor of the Carry On films
taken as written
one's is I'S, I being one, shortened to IS
a faction is a party or group within a larger body

explanation.surface: Someone is sorry James arrived second at a social gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: SID is reversed by 'turning up'. 'one's' is read as I (one) plus 'S.
explanation.definitionFit: Discontent and displeasure with how things turned out is close to regret.

clue.text: Get stick

definitions.meaning: to get means to understand or catch on
a small thin piece of a branch

explanation.definitionFit: To twig is informal for understanding, and a twig is a slender stick from a tree.

clue.text: German dog, setter perhaps, found in local district

parts.note: Hund is the German word for dog
the red setter is a breed of dog, so setter suggests red

explanation.surface: An Alsatian or a gun dog turns up in the neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: A hundred was an old subdivision of an English county; crossword setters also hint at themselves as 'setter'.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically an English shire was divided into hundreds, each a local administrative area.

clue.text: Friendly or dreadfully cold air

indicators.note: dreadfully says the words cold air are treated badly and rearranged

explanation.surface: A choice between a warm welcome and a chilly, unpleasant atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: A cordial manner is warm and friendly, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Yield to pressure to show revealing garment

parts.note: a crop is a harvest or yield
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Giving in to pressure to display a skimpy outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: A short top exposing the midriff is a revealing item of clothing.

clue.text: Anger about embracing the Italian

indicators.note: embracing means holding the other piece inside

parts.note: re means about or concerning
il is the Italian for the

explanation.surface: Fury at someone hugging an Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: To rile someone is to annoy or anger them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Acknowledgement of mistake given doctrines traced incorrectly

indicators.note: incorrectly says the letters of doctrines traced are put in a wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone admits error after tracing beliefs wrongly.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a stock admission that one was wrong.

clue.text: Dregs I would start to empty in sheltered spot

parts.note: lees are the sediment in wine
I'd is short for I would

indicators.note: start to picks the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone finishing the last of the wine decides to drain the bottle somewhere snug.
explanation.definitionFit: The side away from the wind is sheltered, so it is a protected place.

clue.text: Deadly game as routine result is brought about

indicators.note: brought about suggests the words as routine result are turned round into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone describes a lethal pastime whose outcome comes routinely.
explanation.definitionFit: The gamble of firing a revolver with one loaded chamber at one's own head is a lethal game.

clue.text: Return of jackal/fox hybrid prompts criticism

indicators.note: Return of says the hidden letters are read backwards
a hybrid is a cross of two things, so the run is taken across both animal names

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cross between two wild dogs causes people to complain.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'hybrid prompts criticism' as the definition, but only 'criticism' means the answer; 'hybrid' points to letters straddling jackal and fox, and 'prompts' is a link. KALF read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Flak is slang for heavy adverse comment or censure, borrowed from anti-aircraft fire.

clue.text: Decrepit old car found in packing-case

definitions.meaning: slang for a battered, worn-out motor vehicle
a wooden box for shipping goods

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are the same word: a slatted shipping box and slang for a clapped-out vehicle.

clue.text: Dissident with a saint's heart providing accommodation for conservationists

indicators.note: giving lodging to something means holding it inside
the heart of a word is its central letter

parts.note: NT is the National Trust, the British heritage conservation charity

explanation.surface: A rebel with a good heart who gives lodging to environmental campaigners.
explanation.walkthrough: The NT, Britain's National Trust, sits between A and I, the middle letter of 'saint'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is anti is opposed to the establishment, as a dissenter is.

clue.text: Fit of temper that provides an edge?

definitions.meaning: a leather strap used to hone a razor's edge

explanation.definitionFit: Throwing a strop is a tantrum, and a barber's leather strap sharpens blades.

clue.text: Finish pointless parody

indicators.note: pointless says a compass point, here S, is removed

parts.note: a send-up is a parody

explanation.surface: Stop the pointless satire.
explanation.definitionFit: To end up is to finish or come to a final state.

clue.text: Turned out detective's all over the place, wasting time and energy

indicators.note: all over the place means the remaining letters are scattered into a new order
wasting means throwing away these letters from the word

parts.note: the word is used as written, the possessive adding no letter
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An investigator is thrown out after dithering and squandering effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasting' drops T and E from DETECTIVE, leaving DECTIVE, which 'all over the place' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Being turned out of a home is being forcibly removed from it, a synonym.

clue.text: Camera movement hurt sense of style

parts.note: to pan is to swing a film camera sideways
an ache is a dull hurt

explanation.surface: A sweeping shot by a film camera spoils someone's flair.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache is flamboyant confidence and flair, a stylish dash.

clue.text: Fan loves Northern comic

parts.note: a buff is an enthusiast
love is zero in tennis, and O looks like a zero, so two loves give two Os

explanation.surface: An admirer adores a comedian from the north of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A buffoon is a clown or jester, someone acting the fool for laughs.

clue.text: Go on and on about cover of bulky cushion for lounging on

indicators.note: about means placed around the other piece

parts.note: to be a nag is to keep on and on at someone

indicators.note: the cover of a word is its front, its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone keeps complaining about the covering of a large lounge cushion.
explanation.walkthrough: BE A NAG goes around B, the first letter of 'bulky'.
explanation.definitionFit: A large fabric sack filled with polystyrene beads makes a soft floor seat.

clue.text: New rule stopping terrible fellow attaining a blissful state

indicators.note: attaining means reaching or adding on the next piece
stopping means plugging a gap inside the other piece

parts.note: Ivan the Terrible was the Russian tsar

explanation.surface: A new regulation halts a dreadful man reaching serenity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible fellow' is Ivan the Terrible, the Russian tsar.
explanation.definitionFit: In Buddhism, nirvana is the state of perfect peace beyond suffering.

clue.text: Rude about bishop getting ordained finally? It's far from clear

indicators.note: about means placed around the other piece

parts.note: blue jokes are rude or smutty
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: A coarse remark about a cleric being consecrated, leaving things murky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts one piece around another; 'Rude' means smutty, not impolite, and the bishop is his formal title, not a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A blurred image is indistinct, the opposite of sharp or clear.

clue.text: Punch cutting? Cut probably occurred before this

parts.note: a blow is a punch
dry wit is cutting or sarcastic

explanation.surface: A cutting remark, then talk of a haircut beforehand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' is a haircut: styling with a dryer usually follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Styling hair with a handheld dryer typically follows a haircut at the salon.

clue.text: Weary about accepting the writer may be failing

indicators.note: accepting means taking in the other piece
about says the word is turned round

parts.note: tired means weary
the writer is the setter, so me

explanation.surface: A tired author thinks he may be letting readers down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the word for weary backwards, giving DERIT, and 'accepting' takes the writer inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A demerit is a fault or shortcoming, a point against someone.

clue.text: Roguish and dry but not quiet

indicators.note: but not says this letter is left out of the word

parts.note: to parch is to dry out
P is piano, the musical direction for soft

explanation.surface: Someone is cheeky and drily witty yet not reserved.
explanation.definitionFit: An arch look is mischievous and knowing, playfully sly.

clue.text: Issue makes one meditate moodily

definitions.meaning: issue means offspring, a family of young

explanation.definitionFit: A hatch of young birds is a brood, and to sit worrying over something is to brood.

clue.text: Pole lacking in energy to make side

indicators.note: lacking in says a piece is missing from the word that follows

parts.note: steam is power or energy, as in running out of steam
S is the south pole

explanation.surface: A Polish person short on vigour to form a squad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a nationality; it is S, the South Pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A side is a group of players, such as a football eleven.

clue.text: Downhill runners?

parts.note: not athletes but the long runners that slide down snowy slopes

explanation.definitionFit: Long narrow runners strapped to boots carry a person down slopes.

clue.text: Articulate IT worker forming conclusion

indicators.note: articulate means spoken, so the word is said out loud

parts.note: a coder writes software, a computing worker

explanation.surface: An eloquent computer programmer reaches the final part.
explanation.walkthrough: Said in a non-rhotic British accent, CODER and CODA sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A coda is the closing passage of a piece of music.

clue.text: Mate or sailor welcoming kinky goings-on with physical presence

indicators.note: welcoming means taking another piece in

parts.note: a brick is a dependable friend, an old British term of praise
taken as written
a tar is a sailor
S and M, sadomasochism, is kinky sexual activity

explanation.surface: A friend or seaman takes in some racy behaviour, with a bodily presence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcoming' puts the kinky abbreviation inside the run made from mate, or and sailor. The term contrasts a real high-street shop with online trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Bricks-and-mortar describes a business with real buildings rather than one existing only online.

clue.text: He sang jazzily — a god

indicators.note: jazzily suggests the letters of he sang are improvised into a new order

explanation.surface: A man sings in a jazz style about a deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Ganesha is the elephant-headed Hindu deity of wisdom and new beginnings.

clue.text: Spooner's cherished vessel said to be square one

indicators.note: Spooner swaps the opening sounds of two words

parts.note: dear means loved or cherished
a yacht is a sailing vessel

explanation.surface: A muddle-mouthed don speaks of a beloved boat as the starting point.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of DEAR YACHT (said 'yot') to get the phrase, so 'said to be' marks a swap by sound, not spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Since the year dot means since the very beginning, the same starting point as square one.
